ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [m]_q = (1−q^m)/(1−q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k−1} (1−aq^j), let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k, and let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial. Prove that for positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r ≤ d, and for every integer n > 1 with n ≡ 1 mod 2d, we have Σ_{k=0}^{n−1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^(k(d−dk−2r)/2) / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k ≡ [rn]_q q^(r(1−n)/2) mod [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2.

payload.proof_nl:
By assumption, there exist polynomials A(q), B(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B(q),M(q))=1 and
E(q)=M(q)A(q)/B(q).
We are also given that E(q)=F(q)-G(q). Hence
F(q)-G(q)=E(q)=M(q)A(q)/B(q).
To prove F(q) \equiv G(q) mod M(q) in the stated sense, we must exhibit polynomials A'(q),B'(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B'(q),M(q))=1 and
F(q)-G(q)=M(q)A'(q)/B'(q).
But we may simply take
A'(q)=A(q), \quad B'(q)=B(q).
These are polynomials in Z[q], they satisfy gcd(B'(q),M(q))=gcd(B(q),M(q))=1 by the hypothesis, and the displayed identity above gives
F(q)-G(q)=M(q)A'(q)/B'(q).
Therefore the definition of congruence modulo M(q) is satisfied, so F(q) \equiv G(q) mod M(q).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: If a rational function E equals F minus G and E can be expressed as M times a polynomial numerator divided by a polynomial denominator that is coprime to M, then F and G are congruent modulo M in the stated sense, because their difference has such a representation.

for every rational functions E, F, and G in Q(q)
assuming E equals F minus G
assuming there exist polynomials A and B in Z[q] such that gcd of B and M is 1 and E equals M times A divided by B
then F is congruent to G modulo M, meaning there exist polynomials A_prime and B_prime in Z[q] such that gcd of B_prime and M is 1 and F minus G equals M times A_prime divided by B_prime

payload.statement_nl: Let M(q) be a nonzero polynomial in Z[q], and let E(q), F(q), and G(q) be rational functions in Q(q). Assume that E(q) = F(q) - G(q). Assume also that there exist polynomials A(q) and B(q) in Z[q] such that gcd(B(q), M(q)) = 1 and E(q) = M(q) A(q) / B(q). Then F(q) ≡ G(q) mod M(q), where by definition F(q) ≡ G(q) mod M(q) means that F(q)-G(q) can be written as M(q) A'(q) / B'(q) for some polynomials A'(q), B'(q) in Z[q] with gcd(B'(q), M(q)) = 1.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof directly reuses the existing witnesses A and B to satisfy the existential definition of congruence modulo M.
No semantic drift from the lemma sketch or assembly role is present; this is exactly the intended transfer from a divisibility representation of the difference to the congruence statement.

result_payload.reason: The proof is correct and complete: from the assumptions E = F - G and E = M*A/B with gcd(B,M)=1, one immediately gets F - G = M*A/B, so the witnesses required by the congruence definition are simply A' = A and B' = B. This matches the lemma sketch exactly and uses no undeclared or forbidden dependencies.
